drugs.name: Diclofenac
drugs.mechanism_of_action: Binds and chelates both COX-1 and COX-2 isoforms, blocking conversion of arachidonic acid to pro-inflammatory prostaglandins. May also inhibit COX-2-mediated tumor angiogenesis.

box_warnings.description: NSAIDs cause increased risk of serious cardiovascular thrombotic events including Myocardial infarction and Stroke, which can be fatal. Risk may occur early in treatment and may increase with duration of use.
box_warnings.note: Diclofenac is contraindicated in the setting of Coronary artery bypass graft (CABG) surgery.

box_warnings.description: NSAIDs cause increased risk of serious GI adverse events including bleeding, ulceration, and perforation of the stomach or intestines, which can be fatal. These events can occur at any time during use and without warning symptoms. Elderly patients and patients with prior history of Peptic ulcer disease and/or GI bleeding are at greater risk.

parenteral: Mild to severe acute pain (alone or with opioid analgesics)
topical_solution: Pain of osteoarthritis of the knee(s)
transdermal_patch: Acute pain due to minor strains, sprains, and contusions (adults and pediatric patients 6 years and older)
topical_gel: Arthritis pain in hand, wrist, elbow, foot, ankle, knee
ophthalmic: Pain and photophobia after Corneal refractive surgery
Non-chronic post-traumatic inflammation in non-penetrating wounds
rectal_suppository: Post-operative pain in children (short term up to 3 days)

adults.oral_rheumatoid_arthritis: 150 to 200 mg/day in divided doses (50 mg TID or QID)
adults.parenteral_acute_pain: 75 mg IV bolus over 15 seconds; max 150 mg/day
adults.topical_patch: One patch to most painful area twice daily

pediatrics.transdermal_patch_6_years_and_older: One patch to most painful area twice daily
pediatrics.rectal_suppository_post_op: 1-2 mg/kg first dose, then 1 mg/kg TID for max 3 days; max 3 mg/kg/day or 150 mg/day
pediatrics.rectal_suppository_min_age: Do not use in children under 12 months

administration_notes: Use lowest effective dose for shortest duration.
Adjust dose and frequency based on individual patient response.
For injection: ensure patient is well hydrated prior to administration.
Inspect parenteral solutions for particulate matter before use.

contraindications.condition: Known hypersensitivity to Diclofenac or excipients
contraindications.detail: Including anaphylactic reactions and serious skin reactions

contraindications.condition: History of asthma, urticaria, or allergic-type reactions after Aspirin or other NSAIDs

contraindications.detail: Risk of premature closure of ductus arteriosus and prolonged parturition
Potential for serious adverse reactions in lactating infants

contraindications.condition: Active Gastric/Duodenal/Peptic ulcer, active GI bleeding or perforation
Regional Ulcer, Gastritis, Ulcerative colitis, Inflammatory bowel disease
Cerebrovascular bleeding or other bleeding disorders
Severe Hepatic impairment or Active liver disease
Severe Renal impairment (CrCl < 30 mL/min) or deteriorating Renal disease
Moderate to severe renal insufficiency in perioperative period with risk of volume depletion (Parenteral only)
Use on non-intact or damaged skin (exudative Dermatitis, Eczema, burns, wounds) — Topical only

cardiovascular.thrombotic_events: Increased risk of MI and Stroke. Use lowest effective dose for shortest duration.
cardiovascular.post_mi: Avoid in recent MI patients unless benefits outweigh risks; monitor for cardiac ischemia.
cardiovascular.hypertension: May cause new or worsening hypertension. Monitor BP during initiation and throughout therapy.
cardiovascular.heart_failure: Avoid in severe heart failure unless benefits outweigh risks. Monitor for worsening.

risk_factors: Prior history of peptic ulcer disease / GI bleeding
Concomitant use of Corticosteroids, Aspirin, Anticoagulants, SSRIs
strategy: Use lowest effective dose for shortest duration.
Avoid more than one NSAID simultaneously.
Monitor for signs and symptoms of GI ulceration and bleeding.

hepatotoxicity.description: Marked elevations of ALT/AST reported. Severe reactions including liver necrosis, jaundice, fulminant hepatitis, and liver failure (some fatal).
hepatotoxicity.action: Discontinue immediately if abnormal liver tests persist or worsen, or if signs of liver disease develop.
hepatotoxicity.monitoring: Periodic liver function assessment recommended on long-term therapy.

renal.toxicity: Long-term use can cause renal papillary necrosis and other renal injury.
high_risk_patients: Patients taking Diuretics, ACE inhibitors, or ARBs
renal.hyperkalemia: Increases in serum potassium (including hyperkalemia) have been reported even in patients without renal impairment.
renal.action: Avoid in advanced renal disease. Correct volume status before initiating. Monitor renal function during use.

warnings_and_precautions.anaphylaxis: Diclofenac associated with anaphylactic reactions. Contraindicated in patients with history of NSAID-sensitivity.
warnings_and_precautions.asthma: Contraindicated in aspirin-sensitive asthma. Monitor for changes in asthma symptoms in patients with pre-existing asthma.
warnings_and_precautions.skin_reactions: Serious reactions (SJS, TEN, Exfoliative dermatitis) possible. Discontinue at first appearance of rash.
warnings_and_precautions.dress: Drug Reaction with Eosinophilia and Systemic Symptoms (DRESS) reported; can be fatal. Discontinue immediately if suspected.

fetal_toxicity.premature_closure_ductus_arteriosus: Avoid from ~30 weeks gestation and later.
fetal_toxicity.oligohydramnios: Use at ~20 weeks or later may cause fetal renal dysfunction and oligohydramnios. If necessary, limit dose/duration and monitor amniotic fluid.

warnings_and_precautions.hematological: Anemia can occur. Monitor hemoglobin/hematocrit if signs of anemia develop. Risk increased with anticoagulants, Aspirin, SSRIs, SNRIs.

topical_specific.sun_exposure: Avoid natural or artificial sunlight exposure on treated areas (topical solution, gel).
topical_specific.eye_exposure: Avoid contact with eyes. Wash with water/saline immediately if contact occurs.
topical_specific.photosensitivity_gel: Minimize sunlight/UV exposure. Discontinue at first sign of sunburn.

ophthalmic_specific.keratitis: Topical NSAID use may result in Keratitis, corneal thinning, ulceration, or perforation.
ophthalmic_specific.contact_lenses: Do not wear soft contact lenses during treatment. Reinsert no earlier than 15 minutes after use.

clinically_significant: Serious skin reactions (SJS, TEN, Exfoliative dermatitis)

pregnancy.recommendation: Limit dose and duration between 20-30 weeks gestation. AVOID at 30 weeks gestation or later.
risks: Premature closure of fetal ductus arteriosus
Fetal renal dysfunction leading to oligohydramnios

lactation.recommendation: Contraindicated — potential for serious adverse reactions in breastfed infants.
lactation.detail: Diclofenac may be present in human milk.

pediatrics.transdermal_patch: Established for patients 6 years and older.
pediatrics.gel: Not to be used by children (Actinic keratosis is not a pediatric condition).
pediatrics.rectal_suppository: Post-operative analgesia: 1-2 mg/kg initial, then 1 mg/kg TID max 3 days. Do not use under 12 months.

geriatrics.risk: Greater risk for serious cardiovascular, GI, and/or renal adverse reactions.
geriatrics.recommendation: Start at low end of dosing range. Monitor closely for adverse effects and renal function.

reproductive_potential.females: May delay or prevent rupture of ovarian follicles. Consider withdrawal in women with difficulty conceiving or undergoing infertility investigation.
reproductive_potential.males: May produce adverse effects on male reproductive tissues at clinically relevant doses.

renal_impairment.moderate_to_severe: Not recommended (parenteral). Contraindicated in perioperative period with risk of volume depletion.

comorbid_conditions_to_check: Coronary artery disease / history of MI
recommended_additional_inputs: Route of administration (oral, parenteral, topical, ophthalmic, rectal)

cdss_alert_rules.message: Diclofenac is CONTRAINDICATED in the third trimester of pregnancy (≥30 weeks). Risk of premature closure of fetal ductus arteriosus and prolonged parturition.
Diclofenac use between 20-30 weeks gestation may cause fetal renal dysfunction and oligohydramnios. Use lowest effective dose for shortest duration and monitor amniotic fluid if used >48 hours.
Diclofenac is CONTRAINDICATED in breastfeeding women due to potential serious adverse reactions in the infant.
Diclofenac is CONTRAINDICATED in severe renal impairment (eGFR/CrCl < 30 mL/min). Risk of serious renal toxicity.
Diclofenac is CONTRAINDICATED in severe hepatic impairment or active liver disease.

cdss_alert_rules.trigger: cv_history CONTAINS 'CABG surgery' OR comorbid CONTAINS 'Post-CABG'
cdss_alert_rules.message: Diclofenac is CONTRAINDICATED in the setting of CABG surgery.

cdss_alert_rules.trigger: allergy_history CONTAINS 'NSAID allergy' OR allergy_history CONTAINS 'Aspirin hypersensitivity'
cdss_alert_rules.message: Diclofenac is CONTRAINDICATED in patients with known hypersensitivity to NSAIDs or Aspirin (cross-reactivity risk). History of anaphylaxis, urticaria, or asthma exacerbation with NSAIDs/Aspirin is an absolute contraindication.

cdss_alert_rules.trigger: gi_risk CONTAINS 'Active GI ulcer' OR gi_risk CONTAINS 'Active GI bleeding' OR comorbid CONTAINS 'Inflammatory bowel disease'
cdss_alert_rules.message: Diclofenac is CONTRAINDICATED in patients with active GI ulcer, GI bleeding/perforation, or inflammatory bowel disease.
Diclofenac is CONTRAINDICATED in severe uncontrolled heart failure. NSAIDs increase risk of MI, hospitalization, and death in heart failure patients.
Diclofenac is CONTRAINDICATED in patients with known Hyperkalemia.

cdss_alert_rules.trigger: high_risk_meds CONTAINS 'Anticoagulants' OR high_risk_meds CONTAINS 'Aspirin' OR high_risk_meds CONTAINS 'SSRIs' OR high_risk_meds CONTAINS 'Corticosteroids'
cdss_alert_rules.message: Concomitant use of Diclofenac with Anticoagulants, Aspirin, SSRIs, or Corticosteroids significantly increases risk of serious GI bleeding. Monitor closely and consider gastroprotection.

cdss_alert_rules.trigger: high_risk_meds CONTAINS 'ACE inhibitors' OR high_risk_meds CONTAINS 'ARBs' OR high_risk_meds CONTAINS 'Diuretics'
cdss_alert_rules.message: Diclofenac may blunt the antihypertensive effect of ACE inhibitors, ARBs, and diuretics. Monitor blood pressure and renal function.
Elderly patients are at greater risk for serious cardiovascular, GI, and renal adverse reactions with Diclofenac. Start at lowest effective dose and monitor closely.
Alcohol use increases risk of GI bleeding with Diclofenac. Use with caution.
Smoking is a risk factor for GI bleeding with NSAID use. Consider gastroprotective co-therapy.
Diclofenac may exacerbate asthma, particularly in aspirin-sensitive patients. Monitor for changes in asthma symptoms.

cdss_alert_rules.trigger: comorbid CONTAINS 'Heart failure' OR comorbid CONTAINS 'Hypertension'
cdss_alert_rules.message: Diclofenac may worsen hypertension or heart failure. Monitor blood pressure and signs of heart failure.
Avoid Diclofenac in patients with recent MI unless benefits outweigh the risk of recurrent cardiovascular thrombotic events. Monitor for signs of cardiac ischemia.
Significantly elevated liver enzymes detected. Monitor closely; discontinue Diclofenac if liver tests continue to worsen or symptoms of liver disease develop.
Low hemoglobin detected. Diclofenac may cause or worsen anemia through GI blood loss, fluid retention, or effect on erythropoiesis. Monitor CBC.
Diclofenac is CONTRAINDICATED in patients on dialysis due to severe renal impairment.
Moderate renal impairment (eGFR 30-60 mL/min). Diclofenac should be used with caution. Monitor renal function and avoid parenteral route. Use lowest effective dose.
Moderate hepatic impairment: Pharmacokinetics not studied. Use is not recommended with parenteral Diclofenac. Monitor liver function closely.

cdss_alert_rules.trigger: gi_risk CONTAINS 'Prior peptic ulcer disease' OR gi_risk CONTAINS 'Prior GI bleeding'
cdss_alert_rules.message: Prior history of peptic ulcer or GI bleeding significantly increases risk of serious GI events with Diclofenac. Consider alternative therapy or add gastroprotective agent.

cdss_alert_rules.trigger: comorbid CONTAINS 'Coagulation disorders' OR comorbid CONTAINS 'Cerebrovascular bleeding'
cdss_alert_rules.message: Diclofenac is CONTRAINDICATED in patients with cerebrovascular bleeding or other bleeding disorders.

renal_adjustment.note: Contraindicated in severe renal impairment (eGFR < 30 mL/min).

drug_interactions.interaction: Concomitant use of Diclofenac with anticoagulants significantly increases bleeding risk.
drug_interactions.recommendation: Avoid concurrent use; if unavoidable, monitor INR and coagulation status closely.

drug_interactions.interaction: Concomitant use of Diclofenac with anticoagulants significantly increases bleeding risk.
drug_interactions.recommendation: Avoid concurrent use; if unavoidable, monitor coagulation status closely.

drug_interactions.interaction: Concomitant use of NSAIDs/Aspirin increases the risk of serious GI bleeding and ulceration.
drug_interactions.recommendation: Avoid concurrent use; monitor for GI bleeding.

drug_interactions.interaction: Concomitant use of NSAIDs with Corticosteroids increases the risk of GI ulceration and bleeding.
drug_interactions.recommendation: Use caution; consider gastroprotection.

drug_interactions.interaction: Concomitant use of NSAIDs with SSRIs increases the risk of GI bleeding.
drug_interactions.recommendation: Use caution; monitor for signs of GI bleeding.

drug_interactions.interaction: NSAIDs may blunt the antihypertensive effect and increase the risk of nephrotoxicity.
drug_interactions.recommendation: Monitor blood pressure and renal function regularly.

drug_interactions.interaction: NSAIDs may blunt the antihypertensive effect and increase the risk of nephrotoxicity.
drug_interactions.recommendation: Monitor blood pressure and renal function regularly.

drug_interactions.interaction: NSAIDs may blunt the diuretic and antihypertensive effects, and increase the risk of nephrotoxicity.
drug_interactions.recommendation: Monitor blood pressure, fluid balance, and renal function.

drug_interactions.interaction: Diclofenac may reduce renal clearance of Methotrexate, leading to toxic levels.
drug_interactions.recommendation: Monitor Methotrexate levels closely; consider holding NSAID during high-dose MTX.

drug_interactions.interaction: Diclofenac may increase serum Lithium levels by reducing renal clearance.
drug_interactions.recommendation: Monitor Lithium levels closely; adjust lithium dosage.

drug_interactions.interaction: Diclofenac may increase serum Digoxin levels and half-life.
drug_interactions.recommendation: Monitor Digoxin levels and adjust dosage.

drugs.name: Amoxicillin
drugs.mechanism_of_action: Binds to and inactivates Penicillin-binding proteins (PBPs) on the inner membrane of the bacterial cell wall, disrupting peptidoglycan cross-linkage, leading to cell wall weakening and bacterial lysis.

box_warnings.description: Serious and occasionally fatal hypersensitivity (Anaphylactoid) and Severe cutaneous adverse reactions (SCAR) have been reported in patients receiving beta-lactam therapy, including Amoxicillin.

adults_and_pediatrics: Upper respiratory tract infections (ear, nose, throat) — susceptible Streptococcus spp., S. pneumoniae, Staphylococcus spp., H. influenzae
Lower respiratory tract infections — susceptible Streptococcus spp., S. pneumoniae, Staphylococcus spp., H. influenzae
Genitourinary tract infections — susceptible E. coli, P. mirabilis, E. faecalis
Skin and skin structure infections — susceptible Streptococcus spp., Staphylococcus spp., E. coli
Tonsillitis and/or Pharyngitis caused by S. pyogenes (≥12 years)
Septicaemia — H. influenzae, E. coli, P. mirabilis, Streptococcus, S. pneumoniae, S. faecalis, S. typhi
adults_only: H. pylori infection with Duodenal ulcer disease — Triple therapy (Amoxicillin + Clarithromycin + Lansoprazole)
H. pylori infection with Duodenal ulcer disease — Dual therapy (Amoxicillin + Lansoprazole)
prophylaxis: Alpha-hemolytic Streptococci prophylaxis before dental/oral/upper respiratory tract surgery
Bacterial endocarditis prophylaxis in at-risk cardiac conditions

adults_and_pediatrics_over_40kg.upper_RTI_GU_skin_mild_moderate: 500 mg every 12 hours OR 250 mg every 8 hours
adults_and_pediatrics_over_40kg.lower_RTI: 875 mg every 12 hours OR 500 mg every 8 hours

pediatrics_under_40kg_over_3months.upper_RTI_GU_skin_mild_moderate: 25 mg/kg/day divided every 12 hours OR 20 mg/kg/day divided every 8 hours
pediatrics_under_40kg_over_3months.upper_RTI_GU_skin_severe: 45 mg/kg/day divided every 12 hours OR 40 mg/kg/day divided every 8 hours
pediatrics_under_40kg_over_3months.lower_RTI: 45 mg/kg/day divided every 12 hours OR 40 mg/kg/day divided every 8 hours

dosing.adults_and_pediatrics_over_12years_phary: 775 mg once daily within 1 hour after meal for 10 days

adults_H_pylori.triple_therapy: 1000 mg Amoxicillin + 500 mg Clarithromycin + 30 mg Lansoprazole — all twice daily for 14 days
adults_H_pylori.dual_therapy: 1000 mg Amoxicillin + 30 mg Lansoprazole — each three times daily for 14 days

endocarditis_prophylaxis.adults: 3 g orally 1 hour before procedure, then 1.5 g 6 hours after
endocarditis_prophylaxis.pediatrics: 50 mg/kg (not to exceed adult dose) 1 hour before; then 25 mg/kg 6 hours after

parenteral_adults.septicaemia: 1000 mg every 6 hours by slow IV injection or infusion over 30-60 minutes

parenteral_pediatrics_under_20kg.upper_RTI_skin_GU: 20 mg/kg/day in divided doses every 6-8 hours

GFR_10_to_30.oral: 500 mg or 250 mg every 12 hours depending on severity
GFR_10_to_30.parenteral: 1 g initially, then 0.5-1 g every 12-24 hours IV

GFR_under_10.oral: 500 mg or 250 mg every 24 hours depending on severity
GFR_under_10.parenteral: 1 g initially, then 0.5-1 g every 24 hours IV; for E. coli and S. faecalis: 1 g every 12 hours IV

hemodialysis.oral: 500 mg or 250 mg every 24 hours; additional dose during and at end of dialysis
hemodialysis.parenteral: 1 g at end of dialysis, then 0.5-1 g every 12-24 hours IV

renal_dose_adjustments.pediatrics_under_12_weeks: Max 30 mg/kg/day divided every 12 hours (oral) due to immature renal elimination

administration_notes: Take orally at the start of a meal.
Maintain treatment for minimum 48-72 hours beyond symptom resolution.
For S. pyogenes infections: minimum 10 days to prevent acute rheumatic fever.
For IV infusion: dilute to 3% w/v in compatible fluids (Normal saline, Ringer's, Glucose 5%, etc.)

contraindications.condition: Known serious hypersensitivity to Amoxicillin or other beta-lactam antibiotics (Penicillins, Cephalosporins, Carbapenem, Monobactam)

contraindications.detail: High percentage of patients with mononucleosis develop erythematous skin rash with Amoxicillin

contraindications.condition: Trivial infections where antibiotics are not indicated

anaphylaxis.description: Serious and occasionally fatal anaphylactic reactions reported. More frequent with parenteral therapy but also occurs with oral use.
anaphylaxis.action: Inquire about prior hypersensitivity to Penicillins, Cephalosporins, or other allergens before initiation. Discontinue and initiate emergency treatment with Epinephrine, oxygen, IV steroids, airway management if reaction occurs.
anaphylaxis.cross_sensitivity: Cross-reactivity between Penicillins and Cephalosporins reported.

warnings_and_precautions.severe_cutaneous_reactions: SCAR — SJS, TEN, DRESS, AGEP possible. Monitor closely; discontinue if lesions progress.
warnings_and_precautions.mononucleosis: Do NOT administer Amoxicillin to patients with mononucleosis — high incidence of erythematous rash.
warnings_and_precautions.cdad: Clostridioides difficile-associated diarrhea (CDAD) ranging from mild diarrhea to fatal colitis. Consider in patients presenting with diarrhea post-antibiotic use.
warnings_and_precautions.phenylketonurics: Some formulations contain Aspartame (Phenylalanine). Oral suspensions do NOT contain Phenylalanine — safe for PKU patients.
warnings_and_precautions.cardiovascular: Kounis Syndrome (serious allergic reaction resulting in MI) can occur as chest pain associated with allergic reaction to Amoxicillin.
warnings_and_precautions.hematologic: Abnormal prolongation of prothrombin time (increased INR) reported with concomitant oral anticoagulant use. Monitor anticoagulation level.
warnings_and_precautions.renal: Amoxicillin is primarily renally excreted. Dose reduction required in renal impairment. Periodic renal function assessment during prolonged therapy.
warnings_and_precautions.prolonged_therapy: Periodic assessment of renal, hepatic, and hematopoietic functions during prolonged therapy. Elevated liver enzymes and blood count changes reported.
warnings_and_precautions.superinfections: Discontinue and institute appropriate therapy if superinfections with Candida, Aerobacter, or Pseudomonas occur.
warnings_and_precautions.lymphatic_leukaemia: Amoxicillin-induced skin rashes more common in patients with lymphatic leukaemia. Use with caution.
warnings_and_precautions.convulsions: May occur in patients with impaired renal function, high doses, history of seizures, treated epilepsy, or meningeal disorders.
warnings_and_precautions.jarisch_herxheimer_reaction: May occur during Lyme disease treatment — direct result of bactericidal activity. Usually self-limiting.
warnings_and_precautions.crystalluria: High urine concentrations may cause crystalluria, especially with reduced urine output. Maintain adequate hydration. Inspect urinary catheters at intervals.
laboratory_interference: May decrease urinary estriol in pregnant women
May cause false-positive reactions in urine glucose testing
May interfere with protein testing using colorimetric methods
Transient decrease in plasma conjugated estriol, estriol-glucuronide, conjugated estrone, estradiol after administration in pregnant women
warnings_and_precautions.drug_resistance: Use only for proven or strongly suspected bacterial infections to prevent development of drug-resistant bacteria.
warnings_and_precautions.asthma_hay_fever: Special caution in patients with allergic diathesis, bronchial asthma, or hay fever.
warnings_and_precautions.pediatric_caution: Precaution in premature children and neonatal period. Monitor renal, hepatic, and haematological functions.

clinically_significant: Severe cutaneous adverse reactions (SJS, TEN, DRESS, AGEP)
frequency_unknown: Interstitial nephritis (oliguria, proteinuria, hematuria, hyaline casts, pyuria)

miscellaneous: Tooth discoloration (brown, yellow, or gray staining)

pregnancy.oral: No adequate well-controlled studies in pregnant women. Use only if clearly needed.
pregnancy.parenteral: Amoxicillin crosses the placenta. Use when potential benefits outweigh risks.
pregnancy.note: Amoxicillin may decrease urinary estriol in pregnant women (lab interference).

lactation.detail: Penicillins are excreted in human milk. May lead to sensitization of infants. Stop breastfeeding if GI disorders (diarrhea, candidosis, skin rash) occur in the newborn.

pediatrics.general: Safety and effectiveness established for upper/lower RTI, GU, and skin/skin structure infections.
pediatrics.H_pylori: Safety and effectiveness NOT established in pediatrics.
pediatrics.pharyngitis_tonsillitis: Safety NOT established in pediatrics under 12 years.
pediatrics.neonates_infants_under_12_weeks: Renal function not completely developed — elimination of Amoxicillin delayed. Max 30 mg/kg/day divided every 12 hours.
pediatrics.premature_neonatal: Precaution required. Monitor renal, hepatic, and haematological functions.

geriatrics.risk: Risk of toxic reactions may be greater in elderly due to decreased renal function.
geriatrics.recommendation: Monitor renal function. Exercise care in dose selection.

renal_impairment.hemodialysis: Administer additional dose during and at end of dialysis session.
renal_impairment.neonates_infants: Dose modification required in patients 12 weeks or younger.

hepatic_impairment.note: Periodic assessment of hepatic function during prolonged therapy. Elevated liver enzymes reported.

recommended_additional_inputs: Suspected or confirmed organism and susceptibility

cdss_alert_rules.trigger: allergy_history CONTAINS 'Penicillin allergy' OR allergy_history CONTAINS 'Amoxicillin hypersensitivity' OR allergy_history CONTAINS 'Beta-lactam allergy'
cdss_alert_rules.message: Amoxicillin is CONTRAINDICATED in patients with known serious hypersensitivity to Amoxicillin or other beta-lactam antibiotics (Penicillins, Cephalosporins, Carbapenem, Monobactam). Risk of fatal anaphylaxis.
Cross-reactivity between Penicillins and Cephalosporins has been reported. Use Amoxicillin with extreme caution; consider alternative antibiotic. Risk of severe hypersensitivity reaction.
Amoxicillin is CONTRAINDICATED in patients with infectious mononucleosis. High incidence of erythematous skin rash.
Severe renal impairment (GFR < 30 mL/min): Dose adjustment required. Use 500 mg or 250 mg every 24 hours orally depending on severity. Parenteral: 1 g initially, then 0.5-1 g every 24 hours IV.
Moderate renal impairment (GFR 10-30 mL/min): Dose adjustment required. Use 500 mg or 250 mg every 12 hours orally; parenteral: 1 g initially, then 0.5-1 g every 12-24 hours IV.

Hemodialysis: Administer additional dose both during and at end of each dialysis session. Oral: 500 mg or 250 mg every 24 hours + supplemental dose. Parenteral: 1 g at end of dialysis, then 0.5-1 g every 12-24 hours.
Patients under 12 weeks (3 months): Immature renal function delays Amoxicillin elimination. Maximum oral dose: 30 mg/kg/day divided every 12 hours.

cdss_alert_rules.trigger: high_risk_meds CONTAINS 'Warfarin' OR high_risk_meds CONTAINS 'Oral anticoagulants'
cdss_alert_rules.message: Amoxicillin may prolong prothrombin time (increase INR) in patients on oral anticoagulants. Monitor INR closely and adjust anticoagulant dose as needed.
Amoxicillin competes with Methotrexate for renal tubular secretion, decreasing Methotrexate clearance and increasing toxicity risk. Monitor Methotrexate serum levels closely.
Concurrent Allopurinol and Amoxicillin increases risk of rash. Use with caution.
Amoxicillin may increase absorption of Digoxin. Monitor Digoxin levels and consider dose adjustment.
Amoxicillin may reduce efficacy of oral contraceptives by affecting intestinal flora and reducing estrogen reabsorption. Advise patient to use alternative contraception during and after therapy.
Patients with lymphatic leukaemia are susceptible to Amoxicillin-induced skin rashes. Use with caution.

cdss_alert_rules.trigger: comorbid CONTAINS 'Epilepsy' OR comorbid CONTAINS 'History of seizures' OR comorbid CONTAINS 'Meningeal disorders'
cdss_alert_rules.message: Amoxicillin may cause convulsions in patients with renal impairment, high doses, or predisposing factors such as epilepsy, history of seizures, or meningeal disorders. Monitor closely.

cdss_alert_rules.trigger: comorbid CONTAINS 'Asthma' OR comorbid CONTAINS 'Hay fever' OR comorbid CONTAINS 'Allergic diathesis'
cdss_alert_rules.message: Special caution in patients with bronchial asthma, hay fever, or allergic diathesis due to increased risk of hypersensitivity reactions to Amoxicillin.

Amoxicillin (FDA Category B): No adequate well-controlled studies in pregnant women. Use only if clearly needed. Parenteral: Amoxicillin crosses the placenta — use when benefits outweigh risks. Note: may decrease urinary estriol (lab interference).
Amoxicillin is excreted in human milk. May cause sensitization of the infant. Use with caution. Stop breastfeeding if diarrhea, candidosis, or skin rash occurs in the newborn.
Some Amoxicillin formulations contain Aspartame (Phenylalanine). Select oral suspension formulations — they do NOT contain Phenylalanine and are safe for PKU patients.

cdss_alert_rules.trigger: high_risk_meds CONTAINS 'Chloramphenicol' OR high_risk_meds CONTAINS 'Macrolides' OR high_risk_meds CONTAINS 'Tetracyclines' OR high_risk_meds CONTAINS 'Sulfonamides'
cdss_alert_rules.message: Concurrent use of bacteriostatic antibiotics (Chloramphenicol, Macrolides, Tetracyclines, Sulfonamides) may interfere with the bactericidal activity of Amoxicillin. Avoid concurrent use when possible.
Elevated liver enzymes detected. Amoxicillin can cause hepatic dysfunction including cholestatic jaundice and acute cytolytic hepatitis. Monitor liver function; consider discontinuation if worsening.
Elderly patients are more likely to have decreased renal function. Monitor renal function and exercise caution in dose selection.
Jarisch-Herxheimer reaction may occur during Amoxicillin treatment of Lyme disease. This is a direct result of bactericidal activity on Borrelia burgdorferi — usually self-limiting. Reassure patient.
Severe renal failure (GFR < 10 mL/min) / peritoneal dialysis: Extended dosing interval required. Oral: 500 mg or 250 mg every 24 hours. Parenteral: 1 g initially, then 0.5-1 g every 24 hours.
Probenecid decreases renal tubular secretion of Amoxicillin, increasing and prolonging blood levels. Use with caution and monitor for Amoxicillin toxicity.
Safety and effectiveness of Amoxicillin for H. pylori treatment have NOT been established in pediatric patients. Use is not recommended.

cdss_alert_rules.trigger: indication CONTAINS 'Pharyngitis' OR indication CONTAINS 'Tonsillitis' AND age < 12
cdss_alert_rules.message: Safety and effectiveness of Amoxicillin for tonsillitis/pharyngitis have NOT been established in pediatric patients under 12 years. Use not recommended for this indication.

renal_adjustment.note: Severe renal impairment (eGFR < 30 mL/min): Max 500 mg q12h (1000 mg/day).
Severe renal failure (eGFR < 10 mL/min): Max 500 mg q24h (500 mg/day).

drug_interactions.mechanism: Decreases renal tubular secretion of Amoxicillin
drug_interactions.recommendation: Use with caution
drug_interactions.interaction: Increased and prolonged blood levels of Amoxicillin

drug_interactions.mechanism: Abnormal prolongation of prothrombin time (increased INR)
drug_interactions.recommendation: Adjust anticoagulant dose; monitor INR
drug_interactions.interaction: Increased bleeding risk

drug_interactions.recommendation: Use with caution
drug_interactions.interaction: Increased incidence of rash

drug_interactions.mechanism: Amoxicillin affects intestinal flora, reducing estrogen reabsorption
drug_interactions.recommendation: Advise alternative contraception
drug_interactions.interaction: Reduced efficacy of combined oral estrogen/progesterone contraceptives

drug_interactions.mechanism: Interference with bactericidal effects of Penicillin
drug_interactions.recommendation: Avoid concurrent use; use with caution
drug_interactions.interaction: Reduced Amoxicillin efficacy

drug_interactions.mechanism: Penicillins compete with renal tubular secretion of Methotrexate
drug_interactions.recommendation: Monitor Methotrexate levels closely
drug_interactions.interaction: Decreased Methotrexate clearance; increased toxicity risk

drug_interactions.recommendation: Dose adjustment of Digoxin may be necessary
drug_interactions.interaction: Elevated Digoxin levels

drug_interactions.recommendation: Use with caution
drug_interactions.interaction: Reduced blood concentrations of Amoxicillin

drug_interactions.mechanism: Amoxicillin may decrease urinary Estriol in pregnant women
drug_interactions.recommendation: Caution in pregnant women
drug_interactions.interaction: Altered estriol levels

inr.note: Required if patient is on anticoagulants

recommended_additional_inputs_for_comple: Urine output status (for Amoxicillin crystalluria risk)
History of seizures / Epilepsy (for Amoxicillin CNS risk)
Ocular surgery history / corneal disease status (for Diclofenac ophthalmic)
INR / Prothrombin time (for both drugs if on anticoagulants)
